record.paper_title: Ultra-Dense Cell-Free Massive MIMO for 6G: Technical Overview and Open Questions
record.context_brief: Fronthaul routing, processor placement, and quantization
record.original_question: How should a user-centric ultra-dense cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-MMIMO) network dynamically route uplink traffic from access points (APs) to central processing units (CPUs) and downlink traffic from CPUs to APs, place software-defined cluster processors on CPUs with finite computation capacity, and choose fronthaul quantization rates so that dynamic AP-user clusters remain scalable without overloading fronthaul links or computation resources?

evidence.quote: C. How to Dynamically Route Fronthaul Traffic and Quantize Signals?

As discussed in previous sections, since users are served by user-centric clusters of APs that depend on the user locations and are not a priori determined, a requirement for scalability is that APs and CPUs are connected by a flexible fronthaul network, able to route the data traffic between APs and CPUs.
For a given network topology, the load balancing (via routing) and the allocation of computation resources must be jointly optimized.
In order to optimize the UL fronthaul load, a critical aspect is the fronthaul quantization, i.e., the complex samples r u m,k are quantized with a finite number of bits.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a user-centric ultra-dense cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-MMIMO) wireless network composed of:
- a set of access points (APs) indexed by m ∈ {1,…,M}, each equipped with multiple antennas,
- a set of central processing units (CPUs) indexed by c ∈ {1,…,C}, each having a finite computation capacity P_c (measured, e.g., in complex multiplications per second),
- a set of single-antenna users indexed by k ∈ {1,…,K}, each associated with a dynamically chosen user-centric cluster S_k ⊆ {1,…,M} of serving APs whose composition depends on instantaneous user locations and channel statistics and is not fixed a priori,
- a fronthaul network modeled as a capacitated directed graph G = (V,E) connecting APs and CPUs, where each edge e ∈ E has a finite capacity B_e (bits per second).

For each user k, signal processing functions (channel estimation, combining/precoding, decoding/encoding) are performed by a software-defined "cluster processor" π_k that must be placed on exactly one CPU c(k) ∈ {1,…,C}. In the uplink, each AP m ∈ S_k quantizes its received complex baseband sample r^u_{m,k} using q^u_{m,k} ∈ ℤ_{≥1} bits per real dimension and forwards the quantized signal toward CPU c(k) along a route R^u_{m,k} in G; in the downlink, the CPU forwards quantized precoded samples to each AP m ∈ S_k at rate q^d_{m,k}.

Formulate and solve the following joint optimization problem: choose, jointly and dynamically,
(i) the user-centric clusters {S_k},
(ii) the cluster-processor placement c: {1,…,K} → {1,…,C},
(iii) the uplink routes {R^u_{m,k}} and downlink routes {R^d_{m,k}} through G,
(iv) the per-link uplink and downlink quantization rates {q^u_{m,k}, q^d_{m,k}},

so as to maximize a system-level utility (e.g., sum spectral efficiency, or a proportional-fairness utility of per-user achievable rates computed under a chosen information-theoretic model that accounts for quantization distortion via rate-distortion theory), subject to
(a) fronthaul capacity constraints: for every edge e ∈ E, the aggregate uplink plus downlink quantized traffic routed through e does not exceed B_e,
(b) computation constraints: for every CPU c, the total computational load of all cluster processors π_k with c(k) = c does not exceed P_c,
(c) scalability: the per-user complexity, fronthaul load, and computation cost remain bounded as M, K → ∞ with K/M fixed.

Provide either an exact characterization of the optimal policy or scalable approximation algorithms with provable performance guarantees, and identify the regimes in which fronthaul capacity, computation capacity, or quantization distortion becomes the binding constraint.
artifact.category_tag: Network optimization for cell-free massive MIMO
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been partially addressed by recent works that formulate the joint fronthaul routing, cluster-processor placement, and quantization as a mixed-integer linear program, prove existence of an optimal number of ADC quantization bits, and propose scalable multivariate quantization schemes (alpha-parallel and neural MQ) with linear complexity. However, fully joint optimization including dynamic user-centric clustering, routing, processor placement, and quantization under general fronthaul topologies with provable global guarantees and scalability remains incompletely resolved.

status_evidence.claim: Joint load balancing and computation allocation with optimal ADC quantization characterized.

status_evidence.snippet: cluster processor placement and fronthaul traffic routing are jointly optimized with a mixed-integer linear program… effect of fronthaul quantization rates based on rate-distortion theory

status_evidence.claim: Scalable quantization schemes with linear complexity have been designed.
